query: NVIDIA Data Center revenue growth drivers Hopper Ampere AI infrastructure Q2 fiscal 2027
normalized: 2027 ai ampere center data drivers fiscal growth hopper infrastructure nvidia q2 revenue

output.content:
**Q2 FY2027 Data Center performance.** NVIDIA’s Data Center revenue was a record **$89.0 billion** in the quarter ended July 26, 2026, up **18% sequentially** from $75.2 billion and **117% year over year** from $41.1 billion; it represented roughly 93% of company revenue of $96.2 billion. [[1, 2]]

**Immediate revenue driver: Blackwell Ultra ramp, rather than Hopper/Ampere.** Management explicitly attributed the Data Center increase to the ramp of **Blackwell Ultra infrastructure**. [[1]] Hyperscale revenue reached **$49 billion**, growing **13% sequentially**, driven by sustained Blackwell strength. [[3]] Thus, the reported Q2 growth principally reflected cloud customers deploying new-generation AI-factory capacity for training and inference, not a material broad-based revival of older GPU architectures. [[1, 3]]

**Demand broadened beyond hyperscalers.** NVIDIA’s ACIE subsegment—AI-native customers, neoclouds, industrial and enterprise customers, and sovereign AI deployments—grew **25% sequentially** and **138% year over year**. [[1]] Management identified AI natives, enterprises, sovereign customers, and hyperscalers using AI clouds as the end-demand sources behind that increase. [[1]] This diversification is important because it adds buyers of AI infrastructure beyond the largest cloud platforms while hyperscaler spending remains substantial. [[3]]

**Hopper and Ampere: supporting demand, but not the Q2 growth engine.** Hopper’s direct Q2 contribution was constrained: shipments of Hopper products to China were **less than 1% of Data Center revenue**, and management said current Hopper shipments were dilutive to corporate gross margin. [[1, 3]] Nevertheless, NVIDIA had previously indicated that Hopper and much of the six-year-old Ampere product family were sold out in the cloud, evidence that installed-base and lower-tier capacity demand remained tight even as customers transitioned their incremental major deployments to Blackwell/Blackwell Ultra. [[4]] NVIDIA also emphasizes architectural compatibility across its GPUs: model and software-stack optimization for Blackwell benefits Hopper and Ampere, helping preserve their usefulness and supporting a multi-generation installed base. [[4]]

**Why AI-infrastructure revenue can grow faster than GPU units.** NVIDIA is selling a fuller AI-factory stack—GPU/CPU compute, NVLink and InfiniBand or Ethernet networking, systems, and software—rather than merely standalone accelerators. [[3]] Management quantified the resulting revenue opportunity per gigawatt of data-center capacity as roughly **$18 billion for Hopper**, **$25 billion for Blackwell**, and **$40 billion for Vera Rubin**. [[3]] The mix shift toward higher-value, more integrated Blackwell systems therefore raises NVIDIA content per unit of deployed power and helps explain the magnitude of Data Center revenue growth. [[3]]

**Forward read-through.** NVIDIA guided total Q3 FY2027 revenue to **$108.0 billion ±2%**, explicitly assuming **no Data Center compute revenue from China**. [[5]] It expected sequential growth to be led primarily by ACIE Data Center demand, while hyperscale growth was expected to reaccelerate in Q4 and FY2028 as Vera Rubin supply expanded. [[3]] The main constraint was supply rather than demand: management characterized its FY2028 outlook as supply-constrained amid a global AI-infrastructure buildout across hyperscalers, AI labs, enterprises, AI natives, and sovereign customers. [[3]]
